title: The specified inverse-image comparison respects finite coefficient extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and chosen uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism on schemes where $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $F=E,L$ and $W=X,Y$ put $R_{F,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}$ on $R_{F,Y}$-module complexes, with scalar action transported through $c_F:g^{-1}R_{F,Y}\simeq R_{F,X}$, and $\kappa^{g,F}_K:G_FK\to Lg_F^*K$ for the SPECIFIED integral comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). Here $Lg_F^*$ is completed derived pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

Let $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and write $T_W$ for integral scalar extension to $\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Use the natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_K:T_X(Lg_E^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_L^*(T_YK)$$
of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with its canonical tensor and completion comparison (ordinary tensor associativity followed by the strict quotient-tower completion comparisons). For a derived-complete $H$ put $C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ and let $\chi_{W,H}:C_WH\xrightarrow{\sim}T_WH$ be the SPECIFIED completion comparison of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom], followed by $c_E,c_L$, gives
$$b_K:C_XG_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LC_YK,$$
whose local formula is $y\otimes a\mapsto g^{-1}(y_0\otimes a_0)$ when $y=g^{-1}y_0$ and $a=c_L(g^{-1}a_0)$. The inverse image is an exact equivalence [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], so this tensor identification also defines $b$ on derived categories. The objects $G_EK$ and $Lg_E^*K$ are constructible and derived complete [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Define
$$\beta_K=G_L(\chi_{Y,K})\circ b_K\circ\chi_{X,G_EK}^{-1}:T_XG_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LT_YK.$$
Then the specified maps obey
$$\alpha_K\circ T_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}\circ\beta_K$$
in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51 (completed pullback). The displayed compatibility of the specified comparison with coefficient extension is formulated by an agent from def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison(b); this formula is not a claim quoted from Bhatt-Scholze.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$. The comparison definition gives exact transported inverse image. The tensor-model lemma gives the flat-term K-flat complexes $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$, $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X$, and the chain representative $b_P$ of $b_K$, compatible with all quotient transitions. Thus $Q$ represents $C_YK$ and $Z$ represents $C_XG_EK$.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51, for completed pullback; agent calculation from the specified quotient-tower comparisons. This coefficient-extension identity is not a quoted assertion of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: The finite-free comparison gives natural, resolution-independent isomorphisms $\chi_{W,H}:C_WH\to T_WH$ for derived-complete $H$, represented by the quotient augmentation with zero shifted coordinate; $C_WH$ is derived complete. Finite freeness makes $C_W$ termwise tensor on any complex. Hence $\beta_K=G_L(\chi_{Y,K})b_K\chi_{X,G_EK}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. The specified-alpha lemma supplies $\delta_P$ and the actual map $\chi_Y(P):Q\to B(P)$, and identifies $\alpha_K=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})[\delta_P]\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}^{-1}$.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51, for completed pullback; agent calculation from the specified quotient-tower comparisons. This coefficient-extension identity is not a quoted assertion of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: At coefficient field $L$, normalization gives $\kappa_N=\theta_N^{-1}G_L(u_N)$, with $\theta$ resolution independent and natural and $u$ the natural completion unit. For a derived morphism $v:N\to N'$, therefore $Lg_L^*(v)\kappa_N=\theta_{N'}^{-1}G_L(\widehat v)G_L(u_N)=\theta_{N'}^{-1}G_L(u_{N'})G_L(v)=\kappa_{N'}G_L(v)$. Taking $v=\chi_{Y,K}$ gives $Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\kappa_{C_YK}=\kappa_{T_YK}G_L(\chi_{Y,K})$. Resolution independence allows $Q$ for the first comparison and a K-flat re-resolution of $B(P)$ for the second.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51, for completed pullback; agent calculation from the specified quotient-tower comparisons. This coefficient-extension identity is not a quoted assertion of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: The augmentation-cone lemma gives equality of the actual chain maps $\delta_P(a_P^E\otimes S_X)=a_Q^Lb_P$, including their shifted coordinates. Localizing, with Step 3 identifying the specified $\kappa$ representatives, yields $[\delta_P]C_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)=\kappa^{g,L}_{C_YK}b_K$.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51, for completed pullback; agent calculation from the specified quotient-tower comparisons. This coefficient-extension identity is not a quoted assertion of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text:
Precompose by $\chi_{X,G_EK}$. Naturality of $\chi$, Step 2 and Steps 4–3 give
$$\alpha_K T_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)\chi_{X,G_EK}=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})[\delta_P]C_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}G_L(\chi_{Y,K})b_K=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}\beta_K\chi_{X,G_EK}.$$
Cancel this isomorphism to obtain the required identity.
